atoms.a: What material is the lens of the magnifying glass made of?

atoms.b: Glass is ((++see-through not_see-through)). This means that ((++light shadows)) can shine through it. Glass can be either ((++transparent opaque)) or translucent.

hint.text:
Transparent materials allow light to pass through them.

Translucent materials allow some light through, but we can’t see clear shapes through them.

Opaque materials, such as wood and metal, allow no light through at all.

atoms.a: What is another example of a material that can be transparent?

atoms.b: Sometimes, even a magnifying glass doesn’t ((++enlarge reduce)) a surface enough to make its details visible. You need to use a ((++microscope horoscope)) instead.
This picture shows the stem of a plant as seen through a microscope. The various ((++layers slices)) reveal the ((++age smell)) of the plant, like the growth rings of a tree.
To the naked eye, the surface of steel appears very ((++smooth green)). However, if you look at the ((++metal plastic)) under a microscope, you will see that steel is made up of many tiny crystals.

atoms.a: What material is this pan made of?

atoms.b: The metal must be able to withstand high ((++temperatures frequencies)), otherwise the pan would lose its shape and become unusable. This means that it needs to have a ((++high low)) melting point.

The ((++glass wood)) that is used in containers in laboratories also has a high ((++melting_point softness)). This allows it to be held against a ((++naked_flame open_window)) during experiments without melting or warping.

On the other hand, wood, paper and some plastics are examples of materials that ((++change_irreversibly stay_the_same)) when heated. Many plastics melt if they are exposed to too high a temperature. Wood and paper start to ((++burn disappear)) at relatively low temperatures.
